title: The box round the last move, then the dated rule

aliases.name: A56 A dashed box frames the future space

members.role: the page lands on its axes, the projected year already on the axis as the estimate it is (its tick labelled so) - the future's room in view
the actuals draw on their own words, the last move landing on the number the sentence says
on the move's number a dashed box goes round the last actual move's own ink - the box names the move - and leaves as the next sentence opens
the move's number is written by the hand at its datum, clear of the box and of the estimate to come
on the projection's word the dashed, unbloomed estimate draws from the last actual, tagged with its label and tier
as the estimate lands, the dated rule: the year's tick springs into the accent pill and a dashed rule drops the plot's full height at the date - the date printed once, as an estimate

does: A dashed box goes round the last actual move on its number and leaves; then the dashed estimate draws from the last actual and its date springs into an accent pill on the axis.

use_when.act: COMPARES (projecting) - the latest move, carried forward to a date (BRAVOS-USE-WHEN A56, VERIFY.md's rescope)
use_when.shape: a series of actuals whose LAST move the sentence carries forward, and ONE sourced projected point at a named date
use_when.use: the box names the move, the rule names the date ('Last year: a hundred and twenty-one billion. This year they're tracking toward a hundred and fifty.'; BOOM 'could actually continue until June of 2027')
use_when.dont: a box round empty future space (it bounds drawn actual ink only); a box standing when the date lands (it leaves first); an undated or unlabelled projection (E77); a short projection whose dash alone says it
